project.summary: Put one exact branching runtime under real Intelligence search and interactive Study exploration. Select the simplest measured BranchDriver, integrate it into both consumers, and improve it from actual rollout, latency, memory, determinism, and viewer-saf
project.definition: Put one exact branching runtime under real Intelligence search and interactive Study exploration. Select the simplest measured BranchDriver, integrate it into both consumers, and improve it from actual rollout, latency, memory, determinism, and viewer-safety observations rather than benchmark-only representation work.

krs.text: One selected BranchDriver runs an actual Intelligence teacher workload on the curated matchup with exact baseline-equivalent outcomes, no source or sibling mutation, and recorded whole-search throughput, p50/p95 decision latency, and peak RSS.

From a historical viewer-safe StudyIdentity, the runtime forks authoritative state, executes normal structured Commands, emits canonical events and offers, and returns in one action to an identical source state hash, event cursor, offer, and viewer projection.

The same branch representation supports retained search siblings and ephemeral Study branches, or a measured consumer comparison explicitly justifies two implementations and their shared exactness contract.

Single-worker and saturated consumer measurements establish regression budgets for rollout throughput, interactive fork/apply/return latency, and peak RSS; the budgets run against the production integrations rather than a benchmark-only surrogate.

Search and Study stress runs preserve deterministic replay, object incarnation, nested rollback, viewer-private information, and exact failure reproduction across multiple seeds with zero silent fallbacks to an unmeasured branch path.

task.name: Materialize possible-world batches without re-enumerating support
task.description: INT-17's frozen v1 calibration run exposed an authoritative provider complexity bug. FrozenPolicyLikelihood loops each row in one PossibleWorldSpace and calls root_space.materialize(row); Env.materialize_possible_world currently rebuilds PossibleWorldSpace::for_viewer and recursively enumerates the entire support for every row, making one likelihood update O(S^2). At the frozen 121,485-row maximum this is about 14.76B row-enumeration operations per update, and the run stopped after 1h38m with only commitments through ordinal 2. Build the narrow Rules-owned, identity-checked prepared materializer that enumerates one canonical space exactly once per immutable likelihood root and materializes many canonical indices without re-enumeration. The prepared provider object must survive across every inference batch for that root: the proof target is exactly one PossibleWorldSpace::for_viewer construction per likelihood update, not one per row or one per batch. Stream bounded materialized batches and release their isolated Env branches before the next batch; do not retain all S branches simultaneously. Preserve exact ordering, physical-deal weights, viewer-safe identity, source revision and viewer-state validation, deterministic seeded isolated branches, materialization mode semantics, and fail-closed stale or mismatched identity behavior. Migrate FrozenPolicyLikelihood to the production prepared/batch surface and make wall, CPU, and RSS caps observable/checkable between inference batches rather than only after a whole decision ordinal. Prove single-index and batch parity against the existing provider, add debug Rust and uv-managed Python regression coverage including the exact construction call-count plus scaling/peak-RSS evidence, and retain measured complexity and throughput receipts. Do not edit or rerun the immutable INT-17 v1 contract or its failure receipt: the repaired provider necessarily changes engine/source/extension fingerprints. Instead publish the repaired provider receipt and complete runtime identities, then preregister experiments/contracts/int-17-belief-calibration-v2.json. The v2 validator must canonically copy v1's trace, likelihood checkpoint, algorithm, cohort, preflight, metrics, prediction, caps, arena interpretation, and exclusions exactly; refresh only provider_receipt and expected_runtime; preserve identity stream 8d9f46fa86742f323f915ba69bc0007e225415e8fc5504792eac4b49ebae66b6 with zero provider gaps; and fail before generation on any scientific drift. Rerun v2 within the existing 6h and 2GiB caps. Do not change the cohort, thresholds, belief semantics, or move possible-world authority into manabot.

task.name: Make bench_branching source_sha256 reproducible across checkouts
task.description:
W2-198 merged at 09ac3405 with both receipts verifying IN ITS WORKTREE, but NEITHER verifies on merged main. Both fail 'source digest mismatch'. This blocks KR2's 'one REPRODUCIBLE harness' clause: the receipts are unverifiable by anyone except the (now-deleted) worktree that produced them.

MEASURED, not inferred (2026-07-16, at merge commit 09ac3405):

* git diff --stat 2f2781e origin/main => EMPTY. Identical git tree. Both checkouts clean (git status --porcelain => 0 lines).
* Yet source_sha256 differs:
    canonical main /Users/jack/src/manabot          => 549f6738cd5b610ac7a8ee63eea607c0075d8d2890599af360a432cf1739076f
    task worktree  ...implement-compact-clone-plus-undo => ba778d315bf1aab095c8eb5adeea7a0161184f1fc8d7a3c1820cc2c78e46c634
    receipts record ba778d31... (the worktree's), so verify fails on main.
* File counts entering the walk: main 197,361 vs worktree 510.

TWO ROOT CAUSES in scripts/bench_branching.py source_sha256():

1. '.claude' is not in excluded_parts. The canonical checkout nests agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/agent-*/**, so ~197k unrelated files (other branches' full source trees) are hashed as 'source'. Any agent activity anywhere changes the digest.
2. '.git' is excluded only as a DIRECTORY name. excluded_parts filters os.walk's dirnames. In a LINKED git worktree, .git is a regular FILE containing 'gitdir: /abs/path', so it survives into filenames and is hashed -- making the digest depend on the worktree's absolute filesystem path. (Diff of the walk sets shows exactly: only-in-TASK = ['.git']; only-in-MAIN = ['.claude/...'] x197k.)

CONSEQUENCE: source_sha256 binds a receipt to the incidental contents and path of the directory that generated it, not to the source it claims to measure. verify() can never pass on main, in CI, or in a fresh clone. This is the same class of failure that left W2-182's receipt red on main and is why that repair did not stick.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (implementer decides): bind the receipt to the SOURCE, not the working directory. Options: (a) hash the git tree/commit of the tracked, contract-relevant paths (managym/src, managym/tests, scripts/bench_branching.py, docs/benchmarks/search-branching-contract-v1.md, Cargo.lock) via git rather than an os.walk of the filesystem; or (b) keep the walk but restrict it to an explicit allowlist of contract-relevant paths and exclude .claude plus any .git entry whether file or directory. (a) is strictly more reproducible and makes the receipt verifiable from any clone at that commit; it also removes the whole-tree brittleness where an unrelated wave/ doc edit invalidates every receipt.

ACCEPTANCE: at the landing commit, 'uv run scripts/bench_branching.py verify' and 'verify --driver compact_clone_undo/current_game_v1' both pass FROM THE CANONICAL MAIN CHECKOUT (not only from the generating worktree), and re-running them from a second independent checkout of the same commit yields the identical digests. Regenerate both receipts under the corrected scheme. Do NOT change measured workload semantics, fixtures, seeds, or the contract ID; this is a provenance fix, not a re-measurement of the candidates. Keep the serial gate: no page-COW, no representation selected (W2-199 owns those).
